meaning: Paying by holding your phone, watch, or card near a card reader at checkout. You do not swipe or insert anything.
clues: It is a way to pay for things with your phone.
You use it in a store, at the checkout.
You hold your phone close to the card reader instead of swiping or inserting a card.
Your phone sends a short-range radio signal, and you may need to unlock it first.
It has three words. The first starts with T, and the second is just two letters long.
assumes: An in-app purchase happens inside an app
Mobile check deposit is about checks, not shopping

decoys.meaning: Buying something extra inside an app you already have, like a game bonus.
Using your phone's camera to photograph a paper check. The money goes into your bank account without a trip to the bank.
A card you load with money ahead of time. You can spend only what you loaded.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, paying meant counting coins into a hand. Now you wave at the register like a wizard.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: And your phone asks for your face, fingerprint, or passcode first, so a lost phone is not a free shopping trip.
